source_title: ‘Avaraachan & Sons’ OTT release: Where to watch Biju Menon and Sreenath Bhasi’s comedy-drama online - Rep - The Times of India
source_excerpt: Biju Menon's Malayalam film 'Avaraachan & Sons' is reportedly set for an OTT release following its theatrical run. Directed by Amal Sheela Thamby, the family comedy hit the big screens on October 2, 2026.'Avaraachan & Sons' OTT release date and platformNetflix is reportedly the streaming destination for 'Avaraachan & Sons', according to Asianet News Malayalam. The film is expected to arrive on the platform after completing its theatrical run. An official announcement confirming the release date is still awaited.'Avaraachan & Sons' plotThe story follows Avaraachan, a father whose irresponsible choices affect his relationship with his children. His problems begin when a workplace scandal costs him his job. His indifference towards everyday responsibilities further frustrates his sons, adding to the tension at home.The situation worsens when Avaraachan becomes the reason behind his son's marriage proposal falling through. A subsequent confrontation also puts him at risk of facing an attack from local residents. He eventually leaves for his sister Ellikutty's home, where his circumstances begin to change. Biju Menon's unique style of delivering comedy is said to be the main highlight of this Amal Sheela Thamby directorial.Biju Menon, Sreenath Bhasi and Ganapathy lead the castBiju Menon plays Avaraachan, the central character whose behaviour drives the family conflict. Sreenath Bhasi and Ganapathy portray his sons, Jaison and Jaimon, who find it difficult to deal with their father's repeated missteps.Akhila Bhargavan plays Keerthi, Jaison's wife. Amal Sheela Thamby directs the film, which combines a slice-of-life narrative with family comedy and emotional drama. Sajith Purushan handled the cinematography.ETimes review and ratingETimes awarded 'Avaraachan & Sons' 2.5 stars out of 5. However, there are a lot of under-utilised plot points. The film remains very even throughout, moving with the flow without creating too many waves, but with occasional flashes of brilliance that elevate it.
